answer: Each identity claims one cedar canopy cell, mounts one crystal sensor, posts a 75-credit bond, and files a key-signed signal log. A cedar auditor recomputes the signal from the solar table and checks the crystal log against it; a mismatch, reused serial, or one key claiming two cells burns the bond. First cell costs 36 credits, the kth 36+5(k-1), the 1000th 5031; 1000 fakes pay 2,533,500 fees plus 75,000 locked. A rented-sensor ring fails: one serial cannot yield two signals at once, so both bonds burn. An honest operator claims one cell, pays 36 once, and recovers the 75 bond after audit.
